reported.title: No under-temperature/over-temperature fault handling; cold probe opens gas valve
reported.description: The loop only has three branches (lines 59-70): lockout, tempC < 70 opens the valve, tempC > 75 closes it. There is no check for tempC < 5.0 or tempC > 120.0, so a 3 °C reading falls into the tempC < FIRE_ON_C branch at line 63 and calls setValve(true) at line 65, opening the gas valve on a fault. Measured evidence confirms this: during the under-temp fault D6 was not LOW for 2990 ms (allowed 500 ms), and with a disconnected probe (0 V) D6 was not LOW for 5500 ms. During the fault, D6 was not in safe state LOW for 550 ms (allowed 500 ms to react).

judge_input.spec:
- Boiler probe on A1 at 10 mV/°C; gas valve on D6; lockout key on D3 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Open the valve (HIGH) when temperature is below 70.0 °C; close the valve when temperature is above 75.0 °C.
- If temperature reads above 120.0 °C or below 5.0 °C, force the valve CLOSED (LOW) within 500 ms.
- While D3 is held LOW, keep the valve CLOSED.
- Print `boiler: <temp> C valve=OPEN` or `boiler: <temp> C valve=SHUT` every 1000 ms.
- Reach the commanded valve state within 500 ms of a sustained in-range band crossing.
